item.title: Vacancy Notice: In the field of Facility Management
item.description: The post (Local Agent Group II) in the Delegation’s Administration Section is part of a team consisting of 16 people. The European Union Delegation to China are seeking a highly skilled and experienced officer in the field of Facility Management to oversee the efficient operation and maintenance of our facilities. Under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Administration, the ideal candidate will be responsible for ensuring the functionality, safety, and overall well-being of our physical spaces, including office and residential buildings. The successful applicant will play a key role in optimizing operational processes, managing resources, and creating a conducive work environment for employees. The position is offered under a fixed term contract of three and a half (3.5) years, renewable once. Main tasks and duties: 1. Facility Maintenance: Develop and implement a comprehensive maintenance program to ensure the proper functioning of all facilities. Coordinate and supervise maintenance activities, including repairs, renovations, and upgrades. Conduct regular inspections to identify and address potential issues proactively. Support strategic planning related to the Delegation’s long-term infrastructure needs, including scenario analysis and investment planning. 2. Space Planning and Utilization: Optimize the layout and utilization of space to meet organizational needs and accommodate growth. Plan and execute space reconfigurations and furniture allocation needs as required. Ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations in all space planning activities. 3. Vendor Management: Source, negotiate with, procure (e.g. needs definition, market surveys, tendering), and manage relationships with external service providers and vendors. Oversee contracted services, such as cleaning, security, and landscaping, to ensure high standards are maintained. Evaluate vendor performance and initiate improvements as needed. 4. Budget Oversight: Develop and manage the facility budget, ensuring cost-effective operations. Monitor expenses, analyse variances, and implement cost-saving measures without compromising safety and quality. 5. Health and Safety Compliance: 6. Environmental Sustainability: 7. Emergency Response and Business Continuity: 8. Infrastructure Planning and Capital Projects Lead and coordinate the identification, assessment, and selection of new premises in line with operational, technical, and security requirements. Manage building-related projects, including new construction, refurbishment, and fit-out works, from initial planning through to completion and handover. Act as the focal point for external stakeholders, including architects, engineers, contractors, and interior designers, ensuring effective coordination and delivery of projects. Oversee project governance, including timelines, budgets, procurement processes, and quality control, ensuring compliance with applicable rules and standards. Translate operational needs into technical specifications and functional layouts, ensuring optimal space planning and workplace design. Monitor project risks and propose mitigation measures to ensure timely and cost-effective delivery. The base salary will depend on pertinent and verified employment experience, typically starting from CNY 24,317. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days, health insurances, and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be December 2026. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) Bachelor's degree in Facility Management, Engineering (civil, mechanical, electrical), Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field, degrees in Project Management or Real Estate/Property Management can also be considered where combined with relevant professional experience. Minimum 3 years proven experience in Facility Management, Engineering (civil, mechanical, electrical), Architecture, Construction Management. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and Mandarin. Right to residence and work in China. Pass the required pre-recruitment medical exam. Assets / selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) Strong knowledge of facility management principles, health and safety regulations, and environmental sustainability practices. Excellent organizational and planning skills. Exceptional communication and interpersonal abilities. Proficient in using facility management software and tools. Knowledge of CAD software (e.g. AutoCAD) is an advantage. item.title: Team Leader in the Information Integrity & Countering Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Division (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4)
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. Part of the Directorate for Policy Planning and Strategic Communication (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT), the main task of the Information Integrity & Countering Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Division (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4) is to defend the EU’s values and interests by understanding and effectively addressing Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI), including through data monitoring and analysis. The division develops strategies and policy approaches to counter FIMI and advance information integrity, leading the implementation of related policy instruments such as the FIMI toolbox and manages dedicated cooperation structures, including the Rapid Alert System. It contributes to the detection and analysis of FIMI, informing evidence-based countermeasures to FIMI, with a specific focus on FIMI threat actors most relevant to the security of the EU and our partners. It undertakes a number of activities to bolster information integrity and resilience inside and outside the EU, including awareness raising, training, and other forms of public engagement offline and online such as the EUvsDisinfo project. Furthermore, it works closely with the global network of EU Delegations and the EU’s CSDP missions and operations, while building partnerships with key international partners, such as NATO or the G7, and civil society organisations. WE LOOK FOR We are looking for a highly motivated, dynamic, flexible and proactive colleague, with proven expertise in the field of countering FIMI. The successful candidate will be based in the Data Knowledge and Analysis Team in the GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4 Division and will operate horizontally across the GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4 Division, coordinating tasks with other EEAS teams, other EU institutions, Member States, international partners and in close interaction with the GII.GLOBAL.STRAT management. WE PROPOSE The post of a Team Leader position to lead the FIMI Data Knowledge and Analysis Team Leader in the Information Integrity & Countering Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference Division (GII.GLOBAL.STRAT.4). The Team Leader is responsible for : Designing, coordinating and implementing a strategic and operational approach that transforms analytical outputs and data-driven insights into active operational and impactful responses to counter FIMI in coordination with other teams. Coordinating the activities of the EEAS FIMI Situational Awareness Hub, which aims to turn data into high quality analysis and effective responses, ensuring the effective planning, reporting, and administrative coordination of the team's work. The role will contribute to the EEAS's strategic communication efforts and oversee the technical implementation of the FIMI Deterrence Playbook. The standardisation of FIMI detection and analysis and developing and implementing FIMI methodological capabilities (FIMI Exposure Matrix, TTPs analysis, FIMI Deterrence Playbook, OSINT capabilities…), taxonomies and data-sharing standards (STIX), and technical tools (DataScienceLab, AI capabilities, leverage OpenCTI databases…). The position will drive the enhancement of interoperability between internal and external systems, promote the automation of analytical and operational processes, and ensure that FIMI threat analysis is translated into coherent, scalable, and impact-oriented operational responses in support of the organisation's objectives. This position also involves preparing briefings and documentation, capacity-building activities, supporting inter-service coordination, ensuring compliance with internal procedures, monitoring the implementation of work plans and deliverables and overseeing budget planning and contracts management. Key responsibilities will include: Coordinate the implementation and maintenance of FIMI analytical methodologies, taxonomies, data models and interoperability standards (e.g. Information Manipulation Set, TTPs categorisation, STIX…). Oversee the development and integration of technical capabilities supporting FIMI detection and analysis, including OSINT methodologies, AI-enabled capabilities, and technical tools, such as DataScienceLab and OpenCTI. Guide and lead FIMI-related threat analysis capabilities and investigations. Ensure FIMI data integration, information exchange and interoperability across internal and external stakeholders. Coordinate the preparation of technical documentation, reporting and briefings. Coordinate the data-driven implementation of the FIMI Deterrence Playbook linking FIMI Threat analysis to concrete response actions across policy, disruption, law enforcement, sanctions and strategic communication. Monitor the implementation of technical work plans, analytical deliverables, and response operational processes ensuring compliance with established procedures. Assess effectiveness through data-driven evaluation to support EEAS actions and communication. Support administrative and financial management activities, including budget planning and implementation, procurement procedures and contract management, in accordance with applicable financial and administrative rules. Conduct capacity-building activities, presentations, and representing the Division on relevant matters This position is classified as an “Administrator” type of post 1 in the grade bracket AD 5 – AD 12. As temporary agents under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (hereafter, the “CEOS”), the duration of the assignment to the post shall, in principle, be four years dependent on the maximum duration of engagement in the EEAS allowed by their type of contract 2. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: Immediately LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The successful candidate for this position will be appointed in accordance with Article 29(1)(a) and Article 98(1), second subparagraph, of the Staff Regulations (SR) and Article 2(b) of the CEOS. item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The MENA2 Division is responsible for EU policy towards Isarel, the occupied Palestinian territory and the Middle East Peace Process. It coordinates internally, including with Member States and with relevant Commission services and agencies; interacts with civil society and the European Parliament; and leads on institutional engagement with Israel and the Palestinian Authority. To note that the Division encounters an increasingly heavy workload in a politically sensitive geographical area, demanding tasks of various nature, pressing deadlines for a relatively small team, where everyone needs to perform optimally, show high resilience and work as a team player. WE PROPOSE: The EEAS is launching a call for expression of interest for the recruitment of one ASSISTANT (AST3) as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of other servants of the EU in accordance with EEAS Decision Admin(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents. Please note that, candidates who have been engaged by the EEAS as non-permanent servants (temporary and contract agents engaged under Article 3b of the CEOS), will be bound by Decision ADMIN(2023) 24 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 14/07/2023 on the maximum duration of engagement by the European External Action Service of non-permanent staff under successive limited duration contracts of different types, and on the minimum lapse of time between successive contracts under Article 2(e) of the CEOS and repealing the Decision ADMIN(2020) 10 of the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy of 16/07/2020. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: Monitoring and analyzing developments in Israel, the occupied Palestinian territory and the Middle East Peace Process, as well as related developments in the MENA region and the international arena; Contributing to the definition, implementation and communication of relevant EU policies in close coordination with Commission services and Member States; Drafting and contributing to briefings, statements, information for the general public, lines to take for the press, reports and other documents; Ensuring effective coordination and liaison with other EEAS Divisions, EU Delegations and Offices, Commission services, the Council and the European Parliament; Assisting in the preparation of internal and external meetings and high-level visits As required, take on any additional tasks related to the work of the Division. LEGAL BASIS The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (CEOS), in accordance with EEAS Decision ADMIN(2015) 20 on the engagement and use of temporary agents The successful candidate will be offered a contract as Temporary Agent under Article 2(b) of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants (CEOS) at the grade of AST3. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Candidates must meet ALL of the following general and specific conditions on the closing date for online applications : Be a national of one of the EU Member States and enjoy full rights as a citizen; Meet any obligations imposed on him or her by the laws concerning military service; Provide the appropriate character references as to their suitability for the performance of their duties; Have the capacity to work in languages of the CFSP in writing and orally. Post-secondary education attested by a diploma followed by at least 3 years of relevant professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties OR secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education, followed by at least 6 years’ professional experience directly related to the nature of the duties. Candidates who, at the time of the application, are EU officials, independently of their administrative status under Article 35 of the SR, cannot request to be recruited as temporary agents. In the case of applications from EU officials on leave for personal grounds, successful candidates will be reinstated into active employment within the meaning of Article 35(a) of the SR. SELECTION CRITERIA: Candidates should: experience in the field of external relations and on the Middle East region; good understanding of the external relations, internal policies, and rules and procedures of the EU institutions; experience and knowledge of CFSP and CSDP; strong drafting and analytical skills combined with sound judgement; a good sense of initiative and team spirit, and the capacity to perform with accuracy and in a flexible manner a diversity of tasks in a complex institutional environment; Furthermore would be considered as asset. EXPRESSION OF INTEREST AND SELECTION PROCEDURE: The selection procedure will take place in three different and successive steps: 1. Expression of Interest Before submitting their application, candidates should carefully check whether they meet all the eligibility criteria in order to avoid exclusion from the selection procedure. Expressions of interest should be sent by e-mail to the following functional mailbox POL-MENA-2@eeas.europa.eu copying AST-STAFF@eeas.europa.eu For the purposes of the e-mail application, the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: " EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b-AST3-POL.MENA.2-job 171032 " Such an expression of interest must be accompanied by: The deadline for submission of expressions is 21/10/2026 at 12:00 midday (Brussels time). For correspondence concerning the selection procedure, please use the following email address (the e-mail must have in the subject the following title: EoI-HQ(AST)-TA2b- AST3-POL.MENA.2-job 171032 " ) : POL-MENA-2@eeas.europa.eu 2. Additional specific written or oral tests might be organised by the panel. Following a comparative assessment of the merits of the preselected candidates, the selection panel will recommend the name of a candidate to the Authority Authorised to Conclude Contracts of Employment, and possibly, name(s) of other candidate(s) that should be placed on a reserve list valid for maximum 12 months. item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The SG Office supports the Secretary-General in her leadership and overall coordination of the EEAS, ensuring coherence across the Service and alignment with institutional priorities, in close liaison with the Cabinet of the HR/VP. It provides support to the Secretary General including the preparation, coordination, and follow-up of the Secretary-General’s engagements and decision-making. The SG Office manages the Secretary-General’s schedule, coordinates briefings, decisions, and follow-up actions, and ensures the preparation and follow-up of key engagements including inter – institutional meetings, meetings with EU MS as well as internal EEAS matters. It coordinates senior management meetings, facilitates internal and external communication, and maintains day-to-day coordination with other EU institutions, Member States, and relevant external stakeholders. WE LOOK FOR: A dynamic, proactive and highly motivated colleague with very good communication and organisational skills and with a developed sense of service. No LC2026/03 The EUSR will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure by telephone. Please address any queries concerning this procedure or related to employment conditions and benefits to delegation-bosnia-and-herzegovina-eusr-personnel@eeas.europa.eu --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Note: Short-listed candidates will be asked to take an interview. Candidates who passed the interview will be invited for a testing. Deadline for application: 22 November 2026 at 23:59 hrs (Brussels time). Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted. Thank you for your interest. Terms of Reference Position Title: Driver Position reference number: LC 2026/03 Direct Supervisor: Head of Finance and Administration ( Salary grade: Grade V (Local Staff Salary Grid) Duty Station: Sarajevo Job Purpose The incumbent will provide safe, reliable and professional driving and related logistical support services to the EUSR team and official visitors, ensuring the proper use, maintenance and availability of assigned vehicles and appropriate reporting to the Head of Administration and Finance. The incumbent will report to the Head of Administration and Finance and Senior Procurement and Logistics Officer, through his/her assigned delegate, and will ensure consistent service delivery to the EUSR team. Typical Duties and Responsibilities Providing safe, reliable and professional driving services using a light-duty motor vehicle (passenger vehicle, light truck, small bus) on general assignments, in all types of weather conditions, within Bosnia and Herzegovina and to neighboring countries on official missions, to transport staff and visiting personnel; Professionally representing the EUSR BiH through responsible and safe driving, appropriate conduct and wearing the approved uniform; Supporting the day-to-day management of the EUSR vehicle fleet through regular physical and data checks; monitoring and anticipating maintenance, tyre replacement, insurance and vehicle registration requirements; consolidating fleet records; reporting anomalies or issues to both the SPLO and the HoFA together with proposed follow-up action; and preparing the procurement documentation required for fleet-related expenditure. Maintaining appearance of vehicles, inside at all times and outside when conditions permit; and performing minor vehicle maintenance and servicing within the limits of the driver's competence; Installing and removing tire chains as required by weather conditions Ensuring that required vehicle documentation, safety equipment and basic supplies are available and reporting any deficiencies to the supervisor; Maintaining vehicle log-books and records detailing official trips, daily mileage, petrol consumption, oil changes etc. Review, scanning for digital archive and filing hard copies of all vehicle logs. Immediately reporting accidents, incidents, vehicle breakdowns or other safety-related issues to the supervisor and completing the required reports in accordance with applicable EUSR procedures and local regulations: Receiving official visitors at the airport, clearly identifying themselves as representing the EUSR BiH, and facilitating immigration and customs formalities; Delivering or collecting documents, materials and light equipment; Coordinating daily driving assignments with the team and ensuring timely availability for scheduled journeys and official visitors; Ensuring compliance with applicable road safety requirements and EUSR procedures, including the appropriate use of seat belts and safe handling of official transportation; Performing other reasonable duties apparent or assigned to him/her. Professional Requirements/Qualifications Completed Secondary Education Minimum seven years' relevant professional experience, preferably including experience with an international organization, diplomatic mission or other multicultural working environment. Technical knowledge of professional driving and basic knowledge of vehicle mechanics. Ability to operate vehicle communication and other relevant communication equipment Good knowledge of routes throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina and familiarity with routes to neighbouring countries. Valid and clean driving license. Experience in driving 4x4 vehicles is essential, defense driving will be advantage. Basic First Aid knowledge. Good knowledge of local traffic laws. Ability to maintain simple records and complete relevant vehicle documentation. Good working knowledge of English and fluent knowledge of one of the official languages of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Availability to work outside regular working hours, including occasional weekends, public holidays and emergency assignments, when required by operational needs. Physical ability to lift and carry materials and light equipment. Competencies and Attributes Ability to take initiative and work in team setting with high sense of confidentiality and flexibility; Ability to operate independently and exercise sound judgement in the performance of assigned duties; Ability to operate within a fast-moving environment and react appropriately to change; ICT skills commensurate with the scope of the post. Very good interpersonal skills to interact within multicultural environment; General conditions The Candidate will need to be certified medically fit for employment by a competent authority/person in BiH. The successful candidate will be required to provide an official Certificate of Criminal Records issued by the competent authorities and hold a valid driving licence with a satisfactory driving history.

item.title: IT SUPPORT ASSISTANT
item.description: VACANCY NOTICE IT SUPPORT ASSISTANT LOCAL AGENT GROUP II Position 354912 – Administration Section We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Democratic Republic of the Congo works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Democratic Republic of the Congo government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. The Delegation of the European Union to the Democratic Republic of the Congo primarily represents the institutions of the European Union in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and conducts political dialogue with the Congolese authorities and civil society to promote shared values and interests, including respect for human rights and political freedoms, the strengthening of democracy and the consolidation of the rule of law. We offer The post of Local IT Support Assistant. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. This is a full-time position (37.5 hours per week) for a Group II local agent, under an indefinite-term contract. The place of employment is the Delegation of the European Union to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Park Towers Building, 6th floor, at the intersection of Batetela and Ambassadeurs Avenues, Gombe, Kinshasa. Occasional atypical hours (evening, weekend), especially when asked to support the RITO or HQ Occasional travel for work missions Work is mainly performed in an office setting. However, it may very rarely involve the operation of heavy equipment (server room equipment such as rack UPS). Under this post, as an IT Assistant, the jobholder works under the supervision of the Head of Administration (HoA) and functional guidance received by the Regional IT Officer (RITO). The jobholder is responsible for providing a range of information technology support roles, including the delivery of end-user support and operational assistance to the RITO and to the EEAS IT HELPDESK (HQ). Interacts with all level of staff in the Delegation and Headquarters, as well as with external stakeholders to provide technical support services and to seek feedback to enhance systems. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: END-USER SUPPORT Prepare and setup IT hardware for newcomers (laptops, mobile phones), based on the HQ reference configuration. These processes use corporate provisioning mechanism and Mobile Device Management (MDM) software. Assist the end-users for office automation tools (Word, Excel, Outlook, etc.) as well as other internal tools. Register user incidents into the ICT helpdesk system and ensure follow-up until their resolution. Install and test optional software and devices upon request by end-users. This can only be done in accordance with the applicable IT corporate guidelines defined by the EEAS. Support and train end-users to the use of presentation and videoconference equipment. Manage the stock of laptops and other accessories (screens, docking stations, keyboards, mouses, various cables, etc.) IT INFRASTRUCTURE Perform the troubleshooting of issues related to IT hardware (laptops, printers, projectors, telephones sets, etc.) Install updates and security patches on software or hardware equipment, in accordance with the instructions of HQ and RITO Setup and manage printers, scanners and “all-in-one” devices, and ensure their maintenance in accordance with the local service providers. Register issues with IT hardware delivered from HQ into the ICT helpdesk system and ensure follow-up and resolution Whenever necessary, perform the disk wiping for all declassified PC’s and decommission them from the inventory before submitting them to the HoA for donation. If required, manage the local PABX and telephones Act as the point of contact for HQ and for local IT/network service providers. Follow-up the hardware problems with ICT material delivered from HQ (laptops, PC’s and videoconference material) – opening – follow-up and closure of incidents with the helpdesk delegations ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT Assist the HoA with the preparation of call for tenders for the purchase of ICT material and/or IT related services based on specifications received by HQ. Assist the HoA and/or RITO in drafting technical requirements and, if necessary, in participating in the technical evaluation of possible options or offers. Assist with the inventory of the Delegation’s ICT equipment. Duties and responsibilities may be adapted according to the evolving needs of the European Union and its diplomatic representations. The base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 01/03/2027. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria Minimum of post-secondary degree or equivalent Post-secondary degree in Information Technology management or similar ( desirable ) Professional certifications in ICT field ( desirable ) Experience in a diplomatic mission, a development agency or in a multi-cultural international setting ( desirable ) Experience working with the European Union policies and procedures ( desirable ) Certificate of good conduct Enjoy civil rights and permits for employment Medically fit to perform the required duties Minimum of 5 years of professional experience as an IT officer, IT technician or similar; Working knowledge (B2) of English and French, and command of the local language(s). Right to residence and work in Democratic Republic of the Congo. Assets/selection criteria Command of the local language(s), command of the French language and working knowledge of English. Communicate effectively and clearly, both orally and in writing Knowledge of information technology and applications, including computer system networks Knowledge of system development workflow and document flow processes Ability to conduct network maintenance and to provide server services and user support Ability to conduct research and gather information from a wide variety of sources Proficient use of standard office information technology tools and systems BEHAVIOURAL ATTRIBUTES Ability to work in a multicultural team, showing good interpersonal skills Ability to adapt quickly and flexibly to new requests Capacity to focus on priorities, to show initiative and to organise own workload in order to respect deadlines Service-oriented mindset Eager to learn and develop new knowledge and competences High degree of integrity, confidentiality and responsibility How to apply The applicant must apply by sending A cover letter in French, signed A Curriculum Vitæ in French , using one of the Europass templates available at: https://europass.europa.eu/fr All documents to the following email address: eeasjobs-118@eeas.europa.eu Please indicate in the email subject line: Name – Position 354912 – Local IT Support Assistant Applications must be received no later than 19 November 2026 at 23:59. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. Depending on the number of applications received, successive phases of Selection may include shortlisting of candidates based assessment of the information provided in the cover letter, CV, practical testing and interviews. item.title: Employment opportunity: Post of Project Officer for Private Sector Development and Investments at the EU Delegation to Pakistan in Islamabad, application deadline 22nd Nov 2026
item.description: The European Union Delegation to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Islamabad is looking for a: Project Manager for Private Sector Development and Investments We are The European Union (EU) is an economic and political partnership between 27 European countries. It plays an important role in international affairs through diplomacy, trade, development aid and working with global organizations. Abroad, the EU is represented through more than 140 diplomatic representations, known also as EU Delegations, which have a similar function to those of an embassy. The EU Delegation to the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, Islamabad was established in Pakistan in 1985 with the objective of fostering closer and stronger ties between the EU and Pakistan, which expanded considerably since. The EU Delegation works in close coordination with the Embassies and Consulates of the 27 EU Member States. We are a fully-fledged diplomatic mission and represent the European Union in dealings with the Pakistani government in areas that are part of the EU’s remit. The EU is a major development cooperation partner of Pakistan, with a portfolio of close to EUR 100 million a year. EU-funded programmes and projects cover a wide range of sectors including rural development and economic growth, climate change and energy, education as well as governance and human rights. In addition, the EU has launched its Global Gateway Strategy. To meet global infrastructure development needs in line with the UN’s Agenda 2030 and its Sustainable Development Goals, its target is to mobilise between 2021 and 2027 up to EUR 300 billion of sustainable investments in quality infrastructure. We offer We are looking for a Project Manager for Private Sector Development and Investments (Local Agent Group 1) in the Delegation’s Partnership Section. Under this post, the recruited person will be attributed functions depending on the needs of the Delegation, and on the changes of these needs. The successful candidate will, in close cooperation with and under the supervision and responsibility of the Head of the Rural Development and Economic Growth section, coordinate and monitor the implementation of ongoing projects in the field of economic growth, private sector development and investments, as well as in the formulation and advancement of new interventions in this field. In addition, we propose an interesting and diverse coordinating role supporting the roll out of the Global Gateway and the implementation of the Team Europe approach and initiatives. Following main tasks and duties are currently required: To advise on and manage projects and programs of development assistance and of financial and technical cooperation with third countries in the fields of economic growth, private sector development and investments; this involves in particular the management of a new programme to support export-oriented SMEs in Pakistan to become more competitive by better complying with evolving green legislation and standards from the EU; To support and contribute to policy dialogue with relevant public and private sector stakeholders in all areas of concern, with a special focus on infrastructure investments; Contribute and prepare inputs to briefings and Global Gateway horizontal issues; Maintain good and effective contacts with the local operators in the field, with the national authorities and institutions, with representatives of the diplomatic missions of the EU Member States as well as of European and International Financial Institutions, with representatives of the principal international donors, with NGOs and other local non-official actors; Prepare and assist in missions from Headquarters; Contribute to communication and visibility of programmes and ad hoc tasks relating to the activities of the Section and the Delegation. The job will be performed in a multicultural environment, based in Islamabad, with a working time of 37.5 hours per week. The team consists of 9 people and there are occasional atypical working hours. The annual base salary will depend on relevant and verified employment experience, typically starting from 7,718,664 PKR. There is a competitive benefits package, subject to certain conditions, including personal leave days and public holidays, health insurances and a retirement savings plan. The expected start date will be 1 January 2027. The duration of the assignment is linked to the duration of the programme on SME competitiveness as outlined above. The duration is initially set for a period of 2 years which is aligned with the full roll-out of the challenge fund from the initial first call for proposals in the textiles in 2026, to the inclusion of all five of the target sectors in 2028. A next phase of the project (year 3) will be marked on the sequential disbursements of funds based on performance throughout 2029. Minimum requirements / eligibility criteria (necessary for the application to be considered) A bachelor’s degree in (agricultural) economics, finance, business administration, public administration, international development, rural development, or similar relevant discipline;. Minimum 6 years professional experience (to be counted as from the qualifying degree), of which at least 3 years in an international organisation, or internationally funded projects; Minimum 3 years professional experience in finance or private sector development (which can be included in the overall 6 years of professional experience); Proven proficiency in understanding, speaking, reading and writing English. Ability to draft documents to high standard essential; High level of general IT literacy, in particular Microsoft Office (word, outlook, excel); Medical fitness to carry out the tasks assigned; Enjoys civil rights and permits for employment under local law; Have a clean criminal record (at the time of the recruitment). Assets / selection criteria (basis for awarding points to select the best applicant) a master’s degree in (agricultural) economics, finance, business administration, public administration, international development, rural development, or similar relevant discipline; Experience in project management, procurement and contract management; Strong knowledge of private sector development, access to finance, financial instruments, investment facilitation, and public-private partnerships; Knowledge of/ experience in international development cooperation; Knowledge of/ experience in EU development cooperation, in particular with relations to Global Gateway is considered a strong asset; Excellent communication, negotiation, and interpersonal skills to engage with diverse stakeholders; Strong organisational and multitasking skills with the ability to manage complex tasks under pressure; A results-oriented approach as well as a highly developed ability to work as a part of a team. How to apply Please send your application and supporting documents exclusively by e-mail to eeasjobs-232@eeas.europa.eu ,, clearly mentioning in the subject: Application – post 113126– name of the applicant . The e-mail must include a cover letter, a detailed CV (preferably in Europass format) and copies of educational transcripts, degrees, experience letters referred to in the application. Applications that are not sent according to the above procedure will not be considered. The deadline for applications is : 22 nd November 2026 The successful candidate will be subject to medical check, background check, and others. The process After the deadline for applications, the eligible applications will be admitted to the Selection by the Committee set up for this purpose. The Selection Committee will prepare a short-list of candidates who are considered to be the most suitable for the post on the basis of a preliminary assessment of the information provided in their application letter and the supporting documents. The short-listed candidates will be invited to an assessment phase, which may include a written test and an interview to assess the suitability of the candidates for the post. Only candidates admitted to each successive selection phase will be contacted individually. The Delegation will use the same means of publication as for this job advertisement to inform the remaining candidates once the recruitment procedure has been completed and that a candidate has (or has not) been recruited. The Delegation will not supply additional information or discuss the selection procedure. During the selection process, please do not contact the members of the Selection Committee, but address your questions and comments to eeasjobs-232@eeas.europa.eu , clearly mentioning in the subject: Request for information – post 113126 – name of the applicant . Requests that are not sent according to the above procedure will not be considered. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES: The European Union is committed to an equal opportunities policy for all its employees and applicants for employment. As an employer, the EU is committed to promoting gender equality and to preventing discrimination on any grounds. It actively welcomes applications from all qualified candidates from diverse backgrounds. We aim at a service which is truly representative of society, where each staff member feels respected, is able to give their best and can develop their full potential. If pre-selected, candidates with disabilities are invited to contact the Delegation eeasjobs-232@eeas.europa.eu , in order to accommodate any special needs and provide assistance to ensure equality of opportunities with other candidates. If a candidate with a disability is selected and recruited, the EEAS is committed to appropriate measures in order to accommodate his or her special needs to the working place or working conditions in accordance with Art 4 of the Decision ADMIN(2025)13 of the Director-General for Resource Management of the European External Action Service on providing reasonable accommodation for local staff with disabilities working in Union Delegations.

item.title: Administrative Agent - Contract Agent FGII - Job No 245682 - EEAS Headquarters - The Sanctions Division
item.description: WE ARE The European External Action Service (EEAS) is the European Union’s diplomatic service. Since 2011, the EEAS carries out the EU’s Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) to promote peace, prosperity, security, and the interests of the EU across the globe. It brings together European civil servants, diplomats from EU Member States, national experts and local staff worldwide. The EEAS supports the High Representative in the exercise of her mandate to steer the Union’s CFSP, including the Common Security and Defence Policy (CSDP), to represent the EU on issues relating to the CFSP and to chair the Foreign Affairs Council. It also supports her as Vice-President of the Commission with regard to her responsibilities within the Commission, including the coordination of other aspects of the EU’s external action. The EEAS works in close cooperation with the EU Member States, the General Secretariat of the Council, the services of the Commission and the Secretariat General of the European Parliament. The EEAS Headquarters are in Brussels. It is also responsible for the management of the network of 145 Union Delegations and Offices worldwide. These Diplomatic Representations play a vital role in representing the EU in the country where they are based, in promoting the values and interests of the EU, and in building networks and partnerships. They are responsible for all policy areas of the relationship between the EU and the host country/organisation. The Sanctions Division supports the EU's Common Foreign and Security Policy and the High Representative through the development, adoption process and maintenance of restrictive measures (sanctions) in pursuit of specific foreign and security policy objectives. In particular: the Division coordinates and contributes to the design of sanctions, prepares and participates in discussions and negotiations regarding sanctions in the Council working groups, drives the process for the adoption of new measures and for the review of the 48 existing EU sanctions regimes, develops sanctions policy, prepares or supports the preparation of listings proposals, coordinates with likeminded countries where relevant, works on increased understanding of sanctions both inside the institutions and outside. The Division works very closely with many services within the EEAS, the Council and Commission in pursuing its mandate. The Sanctions Division is a growing team of 20 colleagues. WE PROPOSE The position of Administrative Agent contract agent FGII as per article 3b of the Conditions of Employment of Other Servants of the European Union (hereafter, the “CEOS”). The Administrative Agent will provide general administrative support to the Division, including document management, internal communication, organisation of meetings and missions, logistic needs and information provision. Subject to having passed the CAST exam, the successful candidate will be offered a contract agent position (Function group II), on the basis of a contract with an initial duration of one year that may be successively renewed up to a maximum duration of six years, subject to the maximum duration of engagement by the EEAS allowed under successive limited duration contracts of different types. PLACE and DATE OF EMPLOYMENT ‎EEAS Headquarters, Brussels, Belgium Post available: 1 February 2027 LEGAL BASIS FOR RECRUITMENT TO THIS POSITION The vacancy is to be filled in accordance with the conditions stipulated under the CEOS, in particular Article 82 thereof. WE LOOK FOR A colleague motivated to join a two-person team providing the administrative support to the Sanctions Division. A dynamic, flexible and proactive colleague with good communication and organisational skills with a developed sense of service. The secretary should be able to quickly adapt to new working environment and be a good team-player. The successful candidate should have good computer skills, a sound knowledge of the standard IT applications and administrative procedures. He/she will be entrusted with the following main tasks: provide efficient secretarial support; carry out various administrative tasks such as diary-keeping, filtering telephone calls, filing and ordering supplies, dealing with correspondence; document management: registration of incoming and outgoing correspondence, including in Ares; organise missions of staff using MIPS application; organise meetings and events; co-ordinate the creation, keeping up to date and retrieval of documents and data in the appropriate files or IT databases; ensure the preparation of briefing files, speeches, etc; coordinate and authorise translation requests. Eligibility criteria Further to the conditions set out in Article 82 of the CEOS, candidates must: have passed a valid EPSO CAST in a valid function group for this post, or be registered in the EPSO Permanent CAST in a valid function group for this post ( https://eu-careers.europa.eu/en/contract-staff-selection-procedures-always-open-registration ). In the latter case, while the registration will make the candidate eligible for the selection procedure, the recruitment of a candidate on this vacant post will be subject to his/her successfully passing the CAST exam; have a level of post-secondary education attested by a diploma or a level of secondary education attested by a diploma giving access to post-secondary education and appropriate professional experience of three year; have the capacity to work in the languages of the CFSP and external relations (English and French) necessary for the performance of their duties; be a national of one of the Member States of the European Union and enjoy full rights as a citizen. Selection criteria Candidates should: have experience in the secretarial field; be well organised with the ability to deal with files in a timely manner; be a flexible and responsible team player with good inter-personal and communication skills; have good written and spoken English; have sound computer skills (MS Office) and good knowledge of standard administrative, workflow based IT applications and administrative procedures. Furthermore: experience of working in a team in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural environment; experience in working with or within other EU institutions; exposure to a secured environment; knowledge of other languages; experience/knowledge in the legal field; will be considered as strong assets. CONDITIONS OF RECRUITMENT AND EMPLOYMENT CONFLICT OF INTEREST AND SECURITY RISKS As a matter of policy, applications by individuals who have dual nationality, of which one of a non-EU country, will be considered on a case-by-case basis taking account in particular of the functions attributed to the vacant post. The EEAS also examines if there could be a conflict of interest or security risks. In this context, all candidates shall fill with their application a declaration of potential conflict of interest ( see attached ). MEDICAL CLEARANCE The signature of the contract will be subject to prior favourable opinion of the Medical Service, unless the successful candidate is a temporary agent currently employed in the EEAS. PERSONNEL SECURITY CLEARANCE (hereafter, “PSC”) The requested level of security clearance for this post is: SECRET UE/EU SECRET. A description of the EU classified information levels is available under Article 2 of Annex A of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . The selected candidate should hold, or be in the position to obtain, a valid Personnel Security Clearance (hereafter, the “PSC”) issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned. Candidates who do not already have a valid PSC will be required to go through the security clearance vetting procedure of their Member State to obtain this clearance in accordance with national laws and regulations and with the procedure laid down in the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025 and in Annex A I of the Decision ADMIN(2023) 18 on the security rules of the EEAS . Until the PSC is issued by the competent authority of the Member State concerned, the selected candidate will not be authorised to access EUCI at the level of CONFIDENTIEL UE/EU CONFIDENTIAL or above, or to participate in any meetings or workflow where EUCI is processed. Please note that the necessary procedure for obtaining a PSC can be initiated on request of the employer only, and not by the individual candidate. In case of failure to obtain or renew the required PSC, the AACC may take the appropriate measures in accordance with Article 7 of the Decision ADMIN(2025) 42 on Implementing Rules and Procedures for Personnel Security measures for protection of EU Classified Information of 20 November 2025. EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES The EEAS strives to be a dynamic, respectful and inclusive Service. We value the talent and professional excellence of our staff, and are committed to building an organisation where gender equality and the respect of diversity are core values, as set out in the EEAS Mission Statement and the EEAS Agenda for Diversity and Inclusion. The EEAS is committed to achieving gender balance within its workforce and strives to avoid any form of discrimination during this selection procedure, as per Article 1(d) of the SR. We actively welcome applications from all qualified candidates without any discrimination based on any ground. We commit to recruit candidates with the highest standard of ability, efficiency and integrity, carrying out a selection based on merits required for the post and from the broadest possible geographical basis among the EU Member States. The EEAS is committed to working with people with disabilities in the terms of the SR. If, by virtue of your medical condition or special needs, you require reasonable accommodation for a part or the entirety of this selection process, please send us an email to CONTRACTAG
